title: Parliament moves to revise terms of service for Parliament staff
what_it_is: A motion moved by the Leader of the House asking Parliament to determine that the terms of service of Parliament staff under the Parliamentary Scheme (2008) and the Language Executive Scheme (Parliament) (2008) be revised in line with the Report of the Commission on Parliament Staff.
why_it_matters: The transcript states that Parliament staff on these two schemes will receive the same salary adjustments of 2% to 9% given to civil servants on the Management Executive Scheme (2008), with effect from 1 August 2026. It also states that a retention payment component will be introduced for Parliamentary Clerks with effect from 1 September 2026. The stated aim is to keep the terms of service of Parliament staff competitive in attracting and retaining officers.

key_points.point: The Leader of the House moved that Parliament determine that the terms of service of Parliament staff be revised in accordance with paragraph 12 of the Commission's Report.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: That this Parliament determines that the terms of service of the staff of Parliament under the Parliamentary Scheme (2008) and the Language Executive Scheme (Parliament) (2008) shall be revised in accordance with paragraph 12 of the Report of the Commission on Parliament Staff in Paper Misc 4 of 2026

key_points.point: The Commission presented its Report to Parliament on 27 July 2026.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: The Commission presented its Report to Parliament on 27 July 2026.

key_points.point: Civil servants on the Management Executive Scheme (2008) were announced to receive salary adjustments of 2% to 9%.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: On 20 February 2026, the Public Service Division (PSD) announced that eligible civil servants on the Management Executive Scheme (2008) would receive salary adjustments of 2% to 9% to keep pace with market standards and enable the Public Service to continue to attract and retain talent to deliver well for Singaporeans.

key_points.point: Those civil service adjustments took effect on 1 August 2026.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: These adjustments took effect on 1 August 2026.

key_points.point: The Commission recommends that the two Parliament staff schemes adopt the same salary adjustments, also from 1 August 2026.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: The Commission recommends that the Parliamentary Scheme (2008) and Language Executive Scheme (Parliament) (2008) adopt the same salary adjustments, also with effect from 1 August 2026.

key_points.point: The Commission recommends a retention payment component for Parliamentary Clerks taking effect from 1 September 2026.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: The Commission also recommends introducing a retention payment component for Parliamentary Clerks under the Parliamentary Scheme (2008), and for this to take effect from 1 September 2026.

key_points.point: The Public Service Division supports the proposals.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)

key_points.point: The Leader of the House asked the House to accept the Commission's recommendations.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: I ask the House to accept the recommendations of the Commission.

key_points.point: Ms Jessica Tan rose in support of the Motion.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
key_points.quote: I rise in support of the Motion moved by the Leader of the House.

key_points.point: The retention payment is described as having a fixed quantum of roughly 1.5 to 1.75 months' salary per year.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
key_points.quote: a fixed quantum, roughly equivalent to 1.5 to 1.75 months' salary per year

key_points.point: The retention payment is described as including annual payouts for entry level Clerks, three-year payouts for those recognised for competence capped at 20 years, and a one-off ex-gratia payment to support the transition.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
key_points.quote: annual payouts for entry level Clerks and three-year payouts for those recognised for competence, but capped at 20 years, and a one-off ex-gratia payment to support the transition

key_points.point: Ms Jessica Tan said recruitment has become more challenging, especially for legally trained officers.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
key_points.quote: Recruitment has also become more challenging, especially for legally trained officers who can handle the specialised nature of Parliamentary work.

key_points.point: Mr Christopher de Souza rose in firm support of the Report.
key_points.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
key_points.quote: I rise in firm support of the Report of the Commission on Parliament Staff

key_points.point: Mr Christopher de Souza described the Report as comprising adoption of the PSD adjustments for the Management Executive Scheme plus higher discretionary bonuses, and a retention payment component.
key_points.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
key_points.quote: first, adopting the same adjustments adopted by PSD for the Management Executive Scheme, as well as higher discretionary bonuses to recognise and encourage strong performance. Second, introducing a retention payment component to attract and retain talent, as set out in paragraph 10 of the Report.

key_points.point: Mr Christopher de Souza urged all Members to support the Motion unanimously.
key_points.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
key_points.quote: I urge all Members to support this worthy Motion unanimously.

key_points.point: The Leader of the House thanked the two Members for their support and urged Members to support the Motion.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: I do not think there is anything further I need to say in response, other than to thank Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Christopher de Souza for their strong support for the Motion and also to urge Members of the House to support the Motion.

key_points.point: The Speaker thanked Members for their support on behalf of his colleagues.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: I would like to thank Members for your strong support on behalf of my colleagues.

not_said: Whether the Motion was put to a vote or carried without a division
Which specific grades or numbers of officers fall under each of the two schemes affected
How the retention payment and the one-off ex-gratia payment will be funded
Whether the salary adjustments and retention payment will be reviewed again, and on what cycle
